'''Zdzislaw I. Pawlak''' (10 November 1926 &ndash; 7 April 2006) was a Polish mathematician and [[computer scientist]]. He was affiliated with several organization, including the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Warsaw School of Information Technology]]. He served as the director of the Institute of Computer Science at the [[Warsaw University of Technology]] (1989–96). Pawlak was known for his contribution to many branches of [[theoretical computer science]]. He is credited with introducing the [[rough set|rough set theory]] and also known for his fundamental works on it.<ref name=commemorate>{{cite journal|last1=Skowron|first1=A.|last2=Peters|first2=J. F.|title=Zdzisław Pawlak Commemorating His Life and Work|journal=Rough Sets and Current Trends in Computing|year=2006|volume=4259|pages=49–52}}</ref> He also introduced the [[Pawlak flow graphs]], a graphical framework for reasoning from data.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Hassanien|last2=Suraj|last3=Slezak|last4=Lingras|title=Rough Computing: Theories, Technologies, and Applications|year=2008|publisher=Information Science Reference}}</ref> He was conferred with [[Order of Polonia Restituta]] in 1999.<ref name=obit>{{cite journal|last=Słowinski|first=R.|title=Obituary|journal=[[Fuzzy Sets and Systems]]|year=2006|volume=157|pages=2419–2422}}</ref> He was also a full member of [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].

==Education and career==
Zdzislaw Pawlak was born on 10 November 1926 in [[Łódź]], [[Second Polish Republic|Poland]].<ref name=obit /> He graduated from a public elementary school in 1939. In 1946 he passed his Baccalaureate Diploma examination, and in 1947 he began studies at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering of the [[Łódź University of Technology]]. Two years later, he moved to the Faculty of Telecommunications at the [[Warsaw University of Technology]]. He received his M.Sc. degree in Telecommunications in 1951, after which he worked in the Institute of Mathematics of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] until 1957.
